15. From a plain reading of .the above provision it is manifestly clear that in the exercise of Revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code the High Court Division will interfere with the judgments, orders and decrees of the Courts subordinate to it provided that the same are not appealable. To put it differently, the Civil Revision petition is incompetent against those judgments/decrees orders passed by the Courts subordinate to it if those are made appealable in the Code itself. 

 20. The plain and simple meaning or construction of the word "thereto" thus is "to that or it or that matter of subject or with regard to that". The language used in section US of the Code clearly demonstrates that the High Court Division shall invoke its jurisdiction only against those orders, judgments and decrees recorded by a Court subordinate to it wherein no appeal lies against these orders, judgments and decrees. Appeal against decree and order has been provided in Order 41 and 43 of the Code respectively. Appeals either against decree or order recorded by the subordinate Courts will lie to the Higher Courts which may be the Court of District Judge and also the High Court Division according to the pecuniary jurisdiction of the suit. The words "no appeal lies thereto" cannot mean no appeal lies only to the High Court Division and not to the Court of District Judge. If the meaning and the construction of the words "no appeal lies thereto" are read in a different way, then possibly there will be violence to the language used in the Act here Act of 1908 (The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908).
